Introduction Purpose: The purpose of this project is to update the Hatchery building’s air-conditioning system. Background: The Hatchery Building was originally constructed in 1962 and consists of unreinforced concrete blocks on concrete stem walls and slab on grade. Exterior and load bearing walls were constructed with 8” blocks with pilasters constructed of 12” block. Non-load bearing walls and short walls utilize 4” and 6” blocks. The roof system consists of open web joists bearing on either masonry walls or wider flanged beams with 5/8” plywood deck and a flat roof. In 1969, an addition was added for lab space on the eastern side of the building. Walls were constructed of 8” block along with open web joists for the roof framing. The SOW requires annual and semiannual oil analysis, oil and refrigerant-filter replacement, and also states that the chillers must be “oilless.” Please clarify which requirements apply to each listed chiller. The two York YMC2 magnetic-bearing chillers are oil-free and do not require compressor oil analysis, oil replacement, or oil-filter replacement. The York YLAA air-cooled chillers and the AAON rooftop unit use sealed compressor and refrigerant circuits; routine oil analysis, oil changes, and external oil- filter replacement are not required unless specified by the applicable manufacturer for the installed unit. The base preventive maintenance price includes inspection, troubleshooting, operational testing, and deficiency reporting for the controls and primary pumps. Repair or replacement is corrective work and requires a separate quote and prior written authorization from the Contracting Officer, unless the item is expressly listed as a preventive maintenance consumable. See the response to Question 2. 2. Is the intent of the contract to include minor and major repairs? What is considered minor and major repairs? No. The base price includes only the preventive maintenance tasks expressly listed in the SOW, associated labor and tools, identified consumables, routine adjustments, reporting, and correction of deficiencies caused by the contractor's own performance or workmanship. Repair or replacement of failed or deteriorated equipment outside those tasks is corrective work and requires an itemized quote and prior written authorization from the Contracting Officer under the applicable NTE CLIN or contract modification. For classification only, a minor repair is limited work that does not require major disassembly or replacement of a major component. A major repair involves substantial disassembly, specialized labor or equipment, opening a refrigerant circuit, structural work, or repair or replacement of a major component. Introduction Purpose: The purpose of this project is to update the Hatchery building’s air-conditioning system. Background: The Hatchery Building was originally constructed in 1962 and consists of unreinforced concrete blocks on concrete stem walls and slab on grade. Exterior and load bearing walls were constructed with 8” blocks with pilasters constructed of 12” block. Non-load bearing walls and short walls utilize 4” and 6” blocks. The roof system consists of open web joists bearing on either masonry walls or wider flanged beams with 5/8” plywood deck and a flat roof. In 1969, an addition was added for lab space on the eastern side of the building. Walls were constructed of 8” block along with open web joists for the roof framing. The SOW requires annual and semiannual oil analysis, oil and refrigerant-filter replacement, and also states that the chillers must be “oilless.” Please clarify which requirements apply to each listed chiller. The two York YMC2 magnetic-bearing chillers are oil-free and do not require compressor oil analysis, oil replacement, or oil-filter replacement. The York YLAA air-cooled chillers and the AAON rooftop unit use sealed compressor and refrigerant circuits; routine oil analysis, oil changes, and external oil- filter replacement are not required unless specified by the applicable manufacturer for the installed unit. For classification only, a minor repair is limited work that does not require major disassembly or replacement of a major component. A major repair involves substantial disassembly, specialized labor or equipment, opening a refrigerant circuit, structural work, or repair or replacement of a major component.
